subject: Helix Systems: clarification on make-whole/onramp offer and pricing makeup
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@helixsys.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing reconciliation and make‑whole ask vs. incumbent

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency/kv cache demo. We're in final commercial discussions with our incumbent (ProcureCorp) and they've tabled a counteroffer that includes a 20% list discount + a two‑quarter service credit to offset migration risk.

I attached a quick TCO worksheet that their finance team sent through; can Redwood entertain a make‑whole style credit (one‑time) + a 12‑month blended rate that gets us cost parity for the first year? Our CFO is pushing for minimal disruption during Q3 budget cycles.

Key asks:
- Baseline blended per‑token price for our expected 150M tokens/month workload
- One‑time migration credit to offset egress and integration effort
- Confirmation of SLA and rollback window for the pilot

If doable, we can fast‑track procurement FYI.

Cheers,
Tom
Director, Cloud Architecture
Helix Systems

Attachment: Helix_TCO_table.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing reconciliation and make‑whole ask vs. incumbent

Rishi / Monica — forwarding Helix's request. They want: (a) blended per‑token for year1 at parity with incumbent, (b) a one‑time migration credit to offset egress/labor.

Quick thoughts: we can be competitive on runtime/unit cost if we recommend combination of small initial prepay + 15% pilot credit. That avoids long‑term list erosion. I mapped estimated monthly spend from their TCO: ~150M tokens/mo => projected $Xk/mo at current Redwood public list depending on quantization profile.

Questions for pricing:
- how big of a one‑time credit do we need to equal their two‑quarter credit? (ProcureCorp's credit is effectively reducing first 6 months by 50% on certain units)
- can we offer a 6‑month pilot credit (not a permanent discount) + a 12‑month commit with a modest tiered stepdown (eg 10% yr1, 5% yr2)?

I want to keep the anchor as a transient make‑whole, not a permanent list reduction. Thoughts?

—Priyom
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing reconciliation and make‑whole ask vs. incumbent

Priyom — flagged a few numbers after running the TCO:
- If we give a one‑time credit equal to ProcureCorp's two quarters, Helix's blended unit becomes too low for our baseline economics unless we constrain it to workloads that hit our dedicated routing.
- Alternative: offer a staged structure: 3 months 40% credit on infra tokens (pilot), 3 months 25% engineering onboarding credit (one‑time), then a 12‑month commit at 12% list discount with a CPI clause. That preserves list and gets them parity for first 6 months.
- Need approval for a backstop cap: $150k one‑time cap and overall minimum 12‑month commit of $1.2M ARR equivalent.

I can sign off on the structure but need Monica on procurement onboarding risk and whether we can guarantee rollback SLA language in the term sheet.

—Rishi
Head of Commercial Operations

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing reconciliation and make‑whole ask vs. incumbent

Agree with Rishi's structure. Two operational items:
1) We can include a pilot rollback window of 14 days, with support for data export hooks, but we need to limit SLA credit exposure to incidents confirmed at our side. Cannot accept open ended rollback liability.
2) The one‑time engineering onboarding credit should be invoiced as a credit note applied to first invoice (keeps accounting clean). Cap at $150k as Rishi suggested.

I'll draft a term sheet snippet for legal and will include the cap + rollback clause.

—Monica
Director, Customer Success Enablement

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@helixsys.com>, ProcureOps <procureops@procurecorp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed make‑whole + pilot structure (draft)

Tom — thanks for the TCO. Based on internal review, here's a draft commercial structure to match the incumbent while protecting both sides:

Proposal (draft):
- Pilot period: 6 months with staged credits
  - Months 1–3: 40% credit on infra tokens (applied to pilot invoices)
  - Months 4–6: 25% engineering onboarding credit (one‑time credit applied to invoice)
- One‑time migration credit cap: $150,000 (Helix must provide invoice evidence for egress if claiming network costs)
- Post‑pilot commitment: 12 months at 12% list discount (with annual CPI adjustment)
- Rollback window: 14 days during pilot with export hooks; SLA credits limited to incidents validated by our ops team
- Deliverables: rollout plan, schedule of sandbox/data handoff, and a mutually signed mutual action plan (MAP)

Attachments: redwood_proposed_term_sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet draft)

If this aligns, we can send a DocuSign for signature and loop legal. If you need movement on the cap, let me know the number the CFO is insisting on and we can evaluate.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@helixsys.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Ops <procureops@procurecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed make‑whole + pilot structure (draft)

Priyom — appreciate the quick turnaround. CFO reviewed and asks if we can stretch the cap to $200k; they argue integration egress estimates are higher. Two small asks:
1) If we accept $150k cap, can we get a 30‑day termination right during months 4–6 (to handle unexpected integration blockers)?
2) Can the onboarding credit explicitly cover up to 80 engineering hours of Redwoods professional services (if used)?

If you can confirm the $150k cap + 30‑day option and the PS hour carveout we should be able to sign this week. We will push back if cap remains strict at $150k.

I'll sign once we have a DocuSign that reflects the PS hour language.

Tom
Director, Cloud Architecture
Helix Systems
